tagline: Morocco's economic capital on the Atlantic — a new marina beneath the Hassan II Mosque anchoring a Rabat–Casablanca–El Jadida coastal water corridor that today only the congested coast road and rail serve.
summary: Casablanca is Morocco's largest city and economic capital, fronting the Atlantic with one of the world's largest artificial harbours (Port de Casablanca) and a modern leisure marina, Marina Casablanca, cut in beside the landmark Hassan II Mosque and the Ain Diab corniche. The city sits at the centre of Morocco's densest coastal axis — Rabat–Salé to the north, Mohammedia's marina town in between, and El Jadida to the south — a corridor carrying the country's heaviest commuter and business travel today by saturated motorway and rail. Demand is business-, commuter- and tourism-led and structurally rising: Mohammed V International Airport, Morocco's primary gateway, handled ~10.4M passengers in 2024 and is being expanded under the Airport 2030 plan, and the whole coast is drawing heavy investment ahead of the 2030 World Cup. A clean foiling-electric layer fits both the short marina-to-corniche and Mohammedia hops (Pioneer II) and the longer open-Atlantic Rabat and El Jadida legs (Quanta-LR), and anchors a flagship North-Africa metro for a demand-platform partner.

use_cases.title: Casablanca ↔ Mohammedia marina hop
use_cases.body: A quiet, zero-wake foiling link from Marina Casablanca up to Mohammedia's marina town, turning a congested coast-road shuttle into a smooth on-water crossing.

use_cases.title: Casablanca ↔ Rabat coastal corridor
use_cases.body: A fast, stable Atlantic sea line between the economic capital and the political capital that bypasses the saturated Casa–Rabat motorway and rail.

use_cases.title: Marina–corniche premium transfers
use_cases.body: Near-silent foiling transfers between Marina Casablanca, the Ain Diab corniche and the Hassan II Mosque waterfront — a clean premium arrival at the heart of the city.

use_cases.title: Casablanca ↔ El Jadida southern leg
use_cases.body: A direct coastal crossing south to El Jadida and the Mazagan resort belt, collapsing a long road drive into a fast sea run.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The short nearshore legs — Marina Casablanca ↔ Mohammedia (~14 nm) and marina/corniche transfers — sit inside the ~70 nm all-electric envelope, with shore charging at the modern marina basin supporting multiple daily rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The open-Atlantic Casablanca ↔ Rabat (~48 nm) and Casablanca ↔ El Jadida (~57 nm) legs run through exposed swell at range edge; Quanta-LR's hybrid range and stability, with no far-end charging dependency, make it the right tool for those lines.

competitive_landscape: Today: saturated motorway and rail on the Casa–Rabat axis, coast-road shuttles, marina day-boats, and the commercial/cruise port; no clean fast-passenger coastal service.
seasonality: Year-round mild Atlantic climate; ocean swell makes a stable foiling hull a comfort and reliability advantage.
regulatory_note: Port de Casablanca is a commercial port under ANP; Marina Casablanca under its marina concessionaire.
